issues.detail: The Hebrew 'עַל מִשְׁפָּטִי אֲכַזֵּב' means 'I would lie against my judgment/right' (i.e., I would be false to my own cause), not '因我的審判，我必使他失敗' ('because of my judgment, I will cause him to fail'). The subject of 'אֲכַזֵּב' is the speaker, not an external 'him'.

The Hebrew 'אָנוּשׁ חִצִּי בְלִי פָשַׁע' means 'my arrow is incurable/desperate without transgression' (i.e., my wound is fatal though I am innocent), not '那無罪的，我卻以箭攻擊' ('the innocent one, I attack with arrows'). The phrase 'בְלִי פָשַׁע' modifies the speaker's condition, not an object being attacked.
